newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut bank announces $150 mln Euro CDs programme.
newsitem.headline: Beirut bank announces $150 mln Euro CDs programme.

text.p: Lebanon's Banque de la Mediterranee said on Thursday it will set up a $150 million Eurodeposit programme through Merrill Lynch International -- the first Euro-CDs to be issued by a Lebanese commercial bank.

Mediterranee, which is Lebanon's biggest bank in terms of assets, said it intended to launch the first tranche of the programme this month in the form of a $50 million issue of two-year Euro certificates of deposit.

"The programme will be the first continuous issuance vehicle established by a Lebanese issuer. The size of the programme will be established for the aggregate amount of $150 million," it said in a statement.
The issue will be lead managed by Merrill Lynch International and Mediterranee Investment Bank, the bank's investment arm.
Mediterranee is 100 percent owned by Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri, a billionaire construction tycoon who since 1992 has spearheaded Lebanon's reconstruction and the revival of its capital markets.
Banking sources said Mediterranee intended through the Euro CDs to be more active in project finance and other types of medium-term finance in Lebanon.
Lebanon suffers from a shortage of medium- and long-term finance since most bank deposits are for only a few weeks.

The statement said Mediterranee intended to establish a benchmark through the first Euro CD issue, enabling it to access the international capital markets for future tranches with maturities ranging from one to five years.
"The programme will allow Mediterranee to access the markets frequently, rapidly and opportunistically, thus increasing the bank's financing flexibility," it added.
It did not give the interest rate on the CDs but other Euro debt instruments issued or to be issued by Lebanese banks are priced several basis points over U.S. treasuries of comparable maturity.

Bank Byblos, one of Beirut's most active banks, has announced a $50 million three-year Euronote issue for September 9 priced at a minimum of 2.75 percent annually over three-year U.S. treasuries as at issue date.

This follows a trailblazing $60 million Eurobond issue in June by Credit Libanais bank, lead managed by Merrill Lynch, which showed the interest of international markets in Lebanese paper despite the clouding of Middle East peace prospects this year.
Mediterranee, which has 24 branches in Lebanon, is also the country's biggest bank in terms of shareholders equity.

Mediterranee said that as of December 31, 1995, it had total assets of $1.94 billion and a capital adequacy ratio of 16.8 percent. It said it had posted profits of $18.9 million and $10.2 million in 1995 and 1994 respectively.
